resolvedSemantics.distance: Haversine with Earth radius 6371 km; output uses nearest integer. As finite-decimal coordinates cannot yield an exact half-integer distance, the mathematical nearest integer is unique. Reference implementation uses half-up as a deterministic convention.
resolvedSemantics.routeOrder: The fixed source implementation computes the rounded integer distance first, then sorts tuples (distance, datacenter name); selection and candidates therefore use this exact lexicographic order.
resolvedSemantics.capacity: REGISTER rejects capacity <= 0; ROUTE increments load only for the selected healthy datacenter when load < capacity.
resolvedSemantics.sourceSample: The three source examples are retained exactly as command sequences and outputs; validation includes nearest-integer, antimeridian, antipodal, duplicate, invalid coordinate, health, name tie and exhausted-capacity cases.
resolvedSemantics.siteInputSupplement: The source omits maximum command count, datacenter count, name grammar and coordinate decimal precision. This candidate explicitly supplies q<=5000, at most 200 datacenters, ASCII identifiers and at most 18 decimal places; commands must have recognized names and correct arity. No production or sandbox verification has been performed.
resolvedSemantics.emptyHealthyCandidates: The Python source formats the no-selection line as `None {names}`; for an empty list this yields `None ` with a trailing space. Candidate statement normalizes the empty candidate list to `None`, recorded as a site-level whitespace normalization.
